attributes.law_screen: claim.law.PP_a-register-only-verdict-cannot-see-a-reassociated-fp-product.20260903.v1 SCREENED AND THE SUSPICION IT RAISES IS REFUTED HERE. The shape looked like PointLineDist2D at first read - target `@0xb0 fmul f1,f3,f1` then `@0xb4 fmul f0,f1,f0` against ours `@0xb0 fmul f0,f1,f0` then `@0xb4 fmul f0,f3,f0` - but tracing the registers back to their definitions shows both streams compute the SAME grouping: target forms (K*n) then (K*n)*S, ours forms (n*K) then S*(n*K), and fmul is exactly commutative, so the two are bit-identical. This is a COMMUTATION, not a reassociation, and the distinction is the whole difference between a source bug and a colour choice. claim.law.T15_register-only-is-an-encoding-verdict-and-never-an-operand-value-verdict.20260903.v1 SCREENED - the identical-slot complement was right to FIRE here and right that the screen alone could not clear it; what clears it is the hand trace above. claim.law.webfrank-pinned-function-source-freeze.20260831.v1 APPLIED - both probes measured on `build/GUNE5D/src/game/anim/.postprocess/body/anim.o`. claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-instruction-count-deltas.20260831.v1 SCREENED and satisfied (106/106 in HEAD and in both probes).
attributes.probed_form: TWO probes, both reverted. HEAD is `info->seqscale = (f32)((f64)*(s16*)(s + 0x22) * lbl_803457C0 * (f64)info->animscale);` at 4 differing words. (1) INNER OPERAND ORDER: -> `(f32)(lbl_803457C0 * (f64)*(s16*)(s + 0x22) * (f64)info->animscale)`. REGRESSED 4 -> 7 words, and it is the informative probe: it FIXED the inner multiply's operand order - ours went from `@0xb0 fmul f0,f1,f0` (n first) to `@0xb0 fmul f0,f2,f0` (K first), which is target's `fmul f1,f3,f1` structure exactly - while shifting the four load destinations by one (magic f2->f1, K f3->f2, n f1->f0) and adding three fresh differing words at +0x90/+0xa8/+0xac. (2) OUTER OPERAND ORDER: -> `(f32)((f64)info->animscale * (lbl_803457C0 * (f64)*(s16*)(s + 0x22)))`. 7 words, and the aligned view over 0x8c:0xc0 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to probe (1)'s - MWCC canonicalises the OUTER commutative multiply, so writing animscale first buys nothing. Two identical A/Bs on the outer operand order; axis dead. HEAD form restored and re-measured at 4 words.
attributes.residual: The rule stays; this record is the source-exhaustion provenance it did not have, plus the clearance the identical-slot complement asked for. THE MECHANISM. Four f64 values are live across 0x90-0xb4: the 0x4330000080000000 int-to-double magic (loaded @0x90), the constant lbl_803457C0 = K (@0x9c), `info->animscale` = S (@0xa4) and the converted `(f64)*(s16*)(s+0x22)` = n (@0xa8). The LOAD ORDER is identical in both streams; only two destinations differ - target puts K in f3 and S in f0, ours puts K in f0 and S in f3 - and the two multiply words follow mechanically from that, because MWCC always places the operand whose register is REUSED AS THE DESTINATION in the rC slot. Target reuses n's register at +0xb0 and S's register at +0xb4; ours reuses K's register at +0xb0 and the intermediate's at +0xb4. So the operand order visible in the instruction is a CONSEQUENCE of the load-destination choice, not an independent source-order fact, which is why the outer spelling is canonicalised away while the inner one is not. What a close needs is S loaded into f0.

held_fixed: One statement, one expression. `info->seqscale`'s assignment at src/game/anim/anim.c:214 was the only text edited; the int-to-double conversion idiom feeding it, the guard `if (*(s16*)(s + 0x22) > 0)`, the `else` arm and the declaration list were constant across both probes. The VALUE was also held fixed by construction: every spelling probed is exactly-equal in IEEE because only commutative fmul operands were permuted, never the grouping.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Read the four load destinations in HEAD and in probe 1. If the block shifts rigidly by one whenever the source changes at all, then the assignment is a function of load ORDER alone and no expression-level edit can permute two of them independently. Measured 2026-09-03: HEAD is magic=f2, K=f0, S=f3, n=f1 and probe 1 is magic=f1, K=f2, S=f3, n=f0 - NOT a rigid shift (S stays at f3 in both while the other three permute), so the destinations are individually reachable and the load-order axis is worth the probe.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the four load destinations, the two multiply operand orders and the reused-register rule were all read from `fnasm.py game/anim/anim InitAnim 0x8c:0xc0 --raw --diff` against the retail bytes, in HEAD and in both probe states.
hypothesis.statement: The reachable lever is which value lands in f0, and the two probes show the inner multiply's source order MOVES the load destinations as a block (probe 1 shifted all four by one) without changing which value is last. The untried axis is to change the number or order of the LOADS rather than the multiply: stage `info->animscale` into an explicit `f64` local read BEFORE the guarded block (so S is loaded first and the magic/K pair follow), or conversely sink the `lbl_803457C0` read into the expression as a literal so only three f64 values are live. Either changes the load sequence the destination assignment is derived from, which the multiply-order axis provably cannot.
